body:
Full-codebase review, server finding 4 of 6. Reproduced with production error handling (TESTING off).

Three call sites use a JSON field without checking its type, so a non-string value is an unhandled HTML 500 instead of the documented JSON envelope:

* `invites.decode_token` — `(token or "").split(...)`: `POST /invites/redeem {"token": 12345}` -> 500 text/html.
* `accounts._require_password` — passes the value to werkzeug: `POST /account/change-password {"current_password": 5}`, `POST /account/change-email`, `DELETE /account {"password": 5}` and both admin step-up routes -> 500 text/html.
* `invites.mint` — `len()`/`EMAIL_RE.match()`: `POST /lists/{id}/invites {"invited_email": 5}` (as a member) -> 500 text/html.

T-116 added exactly this guard to register/login; these were missed. T-236 covers the body SHAPE, not field types, which is why the suite is green. Any authenticated caller can produce a 500 and a stack trace in the log.

Fix direction: type-check before use at the three sites (`invalid_token`, `invalid_credentials`, `invalid_email`), and extend the parametrised request-body tests from body shapes to field types on every route that reads one.
title: A non-string JSON field value is an HTML 500 on five authenticated routes
